key_insight: In laser–TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, laser power, travel speed, and welding current affect molten-pool flow, weld geometry, and arc stability in distinct ways.
engineering_relevance: These parameter–response relationships can guide weld penetration, width, and stability control for Invar tooling used in aerospace composite manufacturing.
method: High-speed photography of pool evolution and arc behavior.
Comparison across laser power, welding speed, and current ranges.
evidence_signal: Across 5–6 kW, 0.5–0.8 m/min, and 150–170 A, higher power increased penetration and arc deflection tendency, higher speed reduced penetration and width while promoting arc deformation, and higher current increased width and arc stability.
watch_item: The abstract reports trends over limited parameter ranges but provides no quantitative prediction errors or validation metrics.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
